exec_last_para: Water tells an interesting - and unexpected - story in South Sudan. GRACE satellites show total water stored in the land rising in all 79 counties (significantly in 76, typically by 3.7 cm a year), and groundwater alone rose in every county too (significantly in 60). Yet the satellite rainfall records do not show a significant trend in any county. The rise fits with floodwater coming down the White Nile after Lake Victoria passed its 1964 record level in 2020, 2021 and 2024. In the 16 Sudd wetland counties, the average flooded area grew from about 2,800 km² in 2018 to 13,200 km² in 2022. Around Bentiu (Rubkona), land that was dry every March until 2020 has been about half under water each March since 2022. IOM recorded about 2.0 million flood displacements in 2020–2025, a third of them in the Sudd counties. In every hunger analysis since 2018, the Sudd counties had 12 to 21 percentage points more people in crisis than the rest of the country. In 2025, the year with the highest average water storage since 2018, the UN aid appeal was 46% funded and US government humanitarian funding fell to less than half of its 2024 level.
